title: Seminar with Alan Kay on Object Oriented Programming (VPRI 0246)
summary: A long recorded seminar in which Alan Kay discusses object-oriented programming, probably from the mid-1980s. He covers the original idea of objects, messaging and the work done at Xerox.
why: HN points to it as primary-source evidence of what Kay meant by objects, which resembled services and message passing rather than modern class-based OOP.

quote.text: Most Alan Kay's presentations I've seen were worth watching. Tons of great ideas in each.
